author: endtransmission
quote:
OK, in short:

Starts off not so great, too easy in most instances and bad balance.
Once the game really gets started it's excellent, so the key is to bare with it.  As a DS fan I was a bit disappointed at first.

It's probably the best Dark Souls game.  Certainly miles better than 2 but we knew that would be the case going in.

Not QUITE as good as Bloodborne but Bloodborne is a legit masterpiece of gaming.  It may end up being From's best game of all time unless they top it with a sequel (surely that's what's next for the team?).

Graphics are a little dull in places early in the game and stunning as you progress.

Some nice shout out and remasters from DS1 that players of the original will enjoy seeing again with current gen graphics.  Some people are complaining about it but for me I love seeing a few familiar bits and pieces brought up to date.

A lot of different enemies, again the balance is a little off and some are too hard and others not hard enough but they'll get the balance right with the next update.

Starts off a little slow with armor sets but gets more interesting as you get into the game.

If you're a souls fan just stick with it.  It pays off once the ball starts rolling but it was a good 10 hours before I really started to enjoy the game as much as Bloodborne or DS1.

author: endtransmission
quote:
Anyone saying this isn't a love letter to Dark Souls are out of their minds.  Yeah it's got Metroid style elements with the paths you can take eventually etc but it's essentially a 2D Dark Souls game.  The good news is it's a really fantastic one.  The only thing I'd change about it, is the art of the humans faces but that's a taste thing, they don't match the quality of everything else in the game.

Few quick plus points:
Challenging but rewarding.
Big game for the price and of excellent quality.
Good system for leveling/skill tree.
Combat is basic yet complex to master due to enemy verity.
Parries.
Invincibility frames rolling.
Looks amazing aside from the faces of humans but you can wear masks.
More obvious weapon leveling system than Dark Souls.

In short:  It's really good.

Best game I've played since Nuclear Throne, Rocket League and Bloodborne.

The only let down is to play online co op is absurdly complex and not just a native thing you can do when you buy the game.  Youtube it to see what I mean.  I'm also knocking a point off for the outrageous amount of Dark Souls in here, even though I love that it is a 2D Souls game.

author: endtransmission
quote: I don't review many games, only if it's a particularly excellent one.  This is one that deserves it.  Very tough (and so rewarding), smooth gameplay and mechanics, nice art style, great music, lots of replayabiity, old school sensibilities with a new fluidity, varied characters that really make you play your playing style, amazing in 1 player and I can't wait to convince a few friends to buy it so we can do a (local) co-op, marking it down one point for not having online multiplayer...  Man, just an excellent, excellent shooter.

author: endtransmission
quote: I love Dark/Demons/Bloodborne, so I don't mind dying (of course) a lot, there are a few moments that feel unfair, and a couple of enemies with especially annoying attack patterns but aside from that, this DLC is fantastic, more of the same excellence.  FROM are just killer game makers, I think they may be the best in the world right now.

author: endtransmission
quote:
Excellent game.  I don't like football games and I don't really like driving games either.  The concept of this game seems so incredibly awkward that you think it can't possibly be enjoyable.

However, play it for a few hours and you're in for a rude awakening:  This game is excellent.

I've spent the last three days playing this with a couple of friends and for a game to sit around on the sofa and play with friends it's hard to beat.  I've not played a better 2 player game on a next-gen console.

Just try it, providing you have patience you'll be rewarded for your efforts.

author: endtransmission
quote:
Excellent game.

The people that are saying this is overpriced are insane.  Every screen, every song, every bit of text: all made very lovingly and bursting with charm.  Great gameplay with simple mechanics but a lot of variety in which to use it - which makes the game fresh at most turns.  It has elements, of:  Dark Souls (Repeating sections to perfection, having to recover your cash), Zelda/Megaman (Equipment, format (in places)), Super Mario World (Music and graphics in places).

Difficulty is actually quite high depending on how you play the game, you can use a standard armour set to increase the difficulty if it's not quite as tough as you'd like.  It's not Dark Souls hard but it's pleasingly difficult.

Story is whatever but the game is all about gameplay and the writing is supernaturally charming and nicely written, taking loving jabs at classic, genre-specific cliches.

Graphics are lovingly made and perfect for the job.

Some people will complain that it's too short but for the money it isn't short at all.  Roughly 10 hours of gameplay on a normal playthrough and then a NG+ option.

In short:  It's the most legitimate homage to old-school gaming I've ever played and to someone like me that's in his early 30s and played games through the NES and SNES era it's a legitimate joy to play.

author: endtransmission
quote:
FROM Japan Studio's masterpiece.  Better than Demon's Souls and Dark Souls (Dark Souls 2 doesn't count of course and isn't a real part of the series, it's like the Mario 2 of the Mario series).

In places it has the best graphics of any game, the sound is fantastic as always, level design is confusing at first as always but once you've completed the game a couple of times you know exactly where you're going and you can just pick and choose your routes with ease.

I'm on my NG+2 at the moment and still going (82 hours of play).  The combat is just such a joy that as with Dark Souls 1 it's not about completing the game once and leaving it, you only get to a really capable level after your first play-through.

Multiplayer's excellent, my personal preference is getting to the end of the game (almost, so all the levels are unlocked) then helping other players out with boss battles but you can go for PVP if that's your preference.

Too much to mention really but the idiots on here giving this a 0 are obviously just haters that bought a X1....  What a stupid choice you made, next time pay attention to what's going on in the industry instead of just buying what you think has a big name.  Anyone that paid even the slightest bit of attention could see that X1 was trash and Microsoft are the evil empire.

Poor misguided fools.

As for the people that made the right choice, rejoice:  This is the first 5 star title of the new generation.  It's about damn time too.  This is BY FAR the weakest generation of games in the history of gaming.

Praise the Moon!

author: endtransmission
quote: VF is a labour of love...  It has a very quick learning curve if you just want to play and an extremely lengthy one if you plan to master it - To put that into context - I've been playing it for over a decade and I'm STILL not that good... but that's part of the charm...  It's like learning to play an instrument, the journey is never ending and infinitely satisfying. It WOULD have been passed over by lesser gamers before the inclusion of an online mode but now these same players will be able to glimpse the heights that can be achieved with the cunning of experience, thought and persistence.  It's simply the best fighter out there and it has been for at least 12 years.  If you don't think so, you haven't played it enough yet.  It's cheap but please don't be if you buy it, become a student of the game, seek knowledge and respect it and it will enrich you as a gamer.
